title: A lazily synced document needs six states, not loading-versus-loaded, and the missing verdict is only assertable after confirming collection membership
content:
ADR 0001 rejects a binary loading flag for a shared, mutating document and defines six states:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `available` | listed, not synced |
| `loading` | backfilling |
| `synced` | caught up, writable |
| `missing` | caught up, a member, nothing materialized |
| `unreachable` | a node exists but no live membership |
| `not-referenced` | unknown |

The distinction that carries the design is **`missing` versus `unreachable`**. `missing` is *membership-authoritative*: it may be asserted only after confirming membership via `getCollectionsForDocuments`. A node that appears in the drive's tree but has no membership is `unreachable`, not missing — which matters because the legacy `powerhouse/document-drive` model's node list can diverge from `document_collections`, and treating a tree entry as authoritative is the divergence bug the ADR is guarding against. That is also why it refuses a combined `DriveMembershipProvider`: routing runs on the uniform `document_collections` index, and only the model-specific tree/existence signal sits behind a thin provider, because combining them would invite using the tree for routing.

Completion is deliberately **channel-level**: `waitForInitialSync(remoteName)` resolves when the initial backfill drains. It cannot come from `SyncStatus`, which is document-keyed and returns `undefined` for exactly the empty/missing case that must be detected — so "initial sync complete" was explicitly dropped as a `SyncStatus` field.

Suspense rides a `LazyReactorClient` decorator over `IReactorClient.get`, injected only when `preloadDocuments:false`, with `document-cache.ts` unchanged — and a hard rule: **never cache a "not-yet" rejection**, or the promise cache is poisoned.
